title: Microsoft Teams: latest meeting experience for anonymous join on Safari and Firefox web
summary: Hold: the briefing treats anonymous-join licensing as unknown even though Microsoft documents the licensing exception for anonymous attendees. It also overstates the join controls as blocking anonymous participants altogether without accounting for separately permitted email-verified participation.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not state the refresh's default on arrival or whether enabling it required action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Safari Firefox anonymous join refreshed pre-join default setting licensing price'. Read roadmap, Learn teams-client-web and anonymous-users-in-meetings. No refresh default found; the documented anonymous-access default concerns admission, not this refresh.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no switch selecting this Safari and Firefox anonymous-join meeting experience.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Safari Firefox latest meeting experience admin policy enable disable refresh pre-join'. Opened Learn anonymous-users-in-meetings, teams-client-web and meeting-policies-overview. Found access and general meeting policies, not a selector for this refresh.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide anonymous-join toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Participants > Anonymous users can join a meeting.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. ... Under Participants, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity <policy name> -DisableAnonymousJoin $true is the documented organisation-wide blocking call.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity <policy name> -DisableAnonymousJoin $true
claims.fix: The cited article prints this exact example, but https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamsmeetingconfiguration says of -Identity: 'The only valid input is Global'. Replace the call in both places with 'Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -DisableAnonymousJoin $true' and cite that reference alongside the article.

claims.claim: The organiser policy toggle is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified toggle Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false prevents anonymous join through that organiser policy.
claims.quote: To prevent anonymous participants from joining meetings organized by users or groups with this policy, use this script: ... Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap item names no licence, add-on or meter.
claims.quote: The latest Teams meeting experiences will be available for Teams on the web in Safari and Firefox browsers - including performance improvements, refreshed pre-join, updated meeting stage, and the updated meeting toolbar. (for anonymous join only)

claims.claim: The cited anonymous-access article names no licence, add-on or meter for merely joining as an anonymous participant.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting anonymous participants license not required join meeting licensing'. Read Learn anonymous-users-in-meetings in full; its licence requirements concern email-code verification, not ordinary anonymous attendance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published the entitlement covering this anonymous-join experience.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' rather than 'unknown' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Begin the licensing notes and section with: 'Microsoft requires organisational users to have a Teams license, except when joining Teams meetings anonymously. Anonymous meeting join is exempt from that requirement; no separate licence or price for this refresh was found.' Replace the open question 'Does any licence apply to this experience?' with 'Will Microsoft publish any licensing terms specific to this refresh?' Keep the separate Teams Premium email-verification qualification.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Safari Firefox anonymous join 329253 latest meeting experience default admin policy license price browser version'. Read Learn user-access, Teams add-on licensing, Teams Premium licensing and anonymous-users-in-meetings; no refresh-specific terms found.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph immediately after table
claims.claim: These controls decide whether anonymous participants can join meetings at all.
claims.quote: If you turn off the organization-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting and Anonymous users can join a meeting after verifying is set to No, anonymous users can't join meetings in your organization.
claims.fix: Replace 'These controls decide whether anonymous participants can join meetings at all.' with 'These controls manage unverified anonymous meeting join; joining after email-code verification is governed separately.' The cited article makes blocking all anonymous participation conditional on the separate verification policy also being set to No.
